lateral-flow.name: Colloidal Gold Lateral Flow Immunoassay
lateral-flow.what: Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) is the technology behind rapid diagnostic tests — a paper-based strip that detects a target analyte via labeled antibodies and capillary flow, producing a visible line within minutes.
lateral-flow.how: A sample is applied to the sample pad and migrates by capillary action through the conjugate pad (where colloidal-gold–labeled antibodies bind the analyte), along the nitrocellulose membrane (where the test and control lines are immobilized), and into the absorbent pad. A visible test line forms when the labeled complex is captured.
lateral-flow.why_matters: It is instrument-free, room-temperature-stable and read by eye — the basis for point-of-care screening across infectious disease, cardiac markers and drug testing. Understanding the components is how buyers evaluate batch consistency and cut-off reliability.
components: Sample pad — receives and pre-treats the sample
Nitrocellulose membrane — test and control lines
applications: Infectious-disease screening (dengue, malaria, HIV, COVID, influenza)
limitations: Qualitative visual readout — faint lines are subjective
Sensitivity may be lower than laboratory methods such as PCR
Matrix effects and nonspecific binding raise background
Limited quantitative capability in visual formats

faq.q: What is colloidal gold lateral flow?
faq.a: An immunochromatographic assay using gold nanoparticles as the visible label on a nitrocellulose strip.

faq.q: Is lateral flow the same as immunochromatography?
faq.a: Lateral flow is the physical format; immunochromatography is the antibody-based recognition mechanism. Most lateral-flow rapid tests are immunochromatographic.

faq.q: How long does a lateral-flow test take?
faq.a: Typically 10–15 minutes to a visible result, depending on the assay.

conjugation.name: Colloidal Gold Conjugation
conjugation.what: Conjugation is the process of attaching detection antibodies to colloidal gold nanoparticles (typically ~40 nm), producing the colored label that makes the test line visible.
conjugation.how: Gold nanoparticles are synthesized and then passively adsorb antibodies via electrostatic and hydrophobic interaction; the conjugate is stabilized, blocked and dispensed onto the conjugate pad. Batch-to-batch control of particle size and antibody density determines signal intensity and consistency.
conjugation.why_matters: Conjugate quality directly affects sensitivity and the clarity of the result line — a key QC point and a common source of batch variation that buyers should ask about.
applications: Signal generation in sandwich and competitive assays
performance_factors: Antibody concentration and pH during conjugation
limitations: Over- or under-loading changes signal intensity

faq.a: Attaching antibodies to gold nanoparticles so they serve as the visible detection label in a lateral-flow test.
It determines signal intensity, line clarity and batch-to-batch consistency.
Antibody concentration, pH, particle size and blocking all affect conjugate stability and performance.

membrane.name: Nitrocellulose Membrane & Test Lines
membrane.what: The nitrocellulose membrane is where the test and control lines are immobilized — the readout zone of a lateral-flow test.
membrane.how: A capture antibody is dispensed at the test line and an anti-species (control) antibody at the control line. As the sample–conjugate complex flows past, it binds at the test line (proportional to analyte) and always binds at the control line (confirming the test ran correctly).
membrane.why_matters: The control line validates each device, and test-line intensity reflects analyte level — understanding this is key to reading results and spotting invalid tests.
components: Membrane pore size — controls flow rate and line sharpness
applications: Immobilization of capture antibodies at test and control lines
Substrate for capillary sample migration in lateral flow
limitations: Humidity and storage affect membrane stability

faq.a: The strip component that immobilizes capture reagents and through which the sample migrates by capillary action.
It controls flow rate and line sharpness, which affect sensitivity and readability.

fia.name: Fluorescence Immunoassay (FIA)
fia.what: Fluorescence immunoassay uses a fluorescent label instead of colloidal gold and is read by a dedicated analyzer, producing quantitative (not just qualitative) results.
fia.how: A fluorescent conjugate binds the analyte and is captured at the test line; a fluorescence analyzer measures the emitted signal intensity, which is converted to a concentration via a calibration curve.
fia.why_matters: FIA upgrades rapid tests from qualitative triage to quantitative measurement — relevant for cardiac markers, hormones and inflammation markers where a numeric result adds clinical value.
applications: Quantitative cardiac and inflammatory markers (troponin, CRP, PCT)
limitations: Reader calibration and QC are required

faq.a: An immunochromatographic assay using fluorescent labels and a reader to produce quantitative or semi-quantitative results.

faq.q: How does FIA differ from visual lateral flow?
faq.a: It uses fluorescent labels read by an instrument, enabling quantification instead of naked-eye line reading.

reagent-dispensing.name: Reagent Dispensing & Line Coating
reagent-dispensing.what: The process of dispensing test and control lines onto nitrocellulose membrane, and conjugate onto the conjugate pad, using precision dispensers.
reagent-dispensing.how: Antibody solutions are applied at a controlled flow rate and line width to produce sharp, uniform lines; conjugate is sprayed onto the conjugate pad before drying.
reagent-dispensing.why_matters: Line sharpness and uniformity directly determine readability and reproducibility — inconsistent dispensing is a primary source of batch-to-batch variation.
applications: Dispensing test and control lines onto nitrocellulose
Spraying conjugate onto the conjugate pad
performance_factors: Dispensing flow rate and line width
limitations: Improper dispensing can damage the membrane

faq.a: Precisely applying test/control-line antibodies onto the membrane and conjugate onto the conjugate pad.
Sharp, uniform lines are easier to read and more reproducible across lots.

drying.name: Drying
drying.what: Controlled removal of moisture from dispensed membranes and pads before assembly.
drying.how: Membranes and pads are dried under controlled temperature and humidity to fix reagents in place without denaturing antibodies.
drying.why_matters: Residual moisture destabilizes reagents and shortens shelf life; overdrying can damage antibodies — both affect lot consistency.

faq.a: It fixes reagents without denaturing them and prevents moisture-related instability.

strip-assembly.name: Strip Assembly & Lamination
strip-assembly.what: Laminating the sample pad, conjugate pad, membrane and absorbent pad onto a backing card.
strip-assembly.how: Pads are overlapped at controlled positions and laminated onto the card; correct overlap drives capillary flow.
strip-assembly.why_matters: Pad overlap and alignment determine capillary flow and reproducible results — misalignment causes flow failure.
applications: Laminating sample pad, conjugate pad, membrane and absorbent pad onto a backing card

faq.a: Laminating the strip components onto a backing card with controlled overlap to drive capillary flow.

cassette-assembly.name: Cassette Assembly
cassette-assembly.what: Cutting laminated cards into strips and loading them into cassettes, panel cups or other housings.
cassette-assembly.how: Cards are cut to width, strips inserted into housings with correct orientation, and each device visually inspected.
cassette-assembly.why_matters: Correct orientation and seating prevent flow failure and invalid results in the field.
applications: Loading strips into cassettes, panels or cups

faq.a: Cutting strips and loading them into housings with correct orientation and inspection.

packaging.name: Packaging & Desiccant
packaging.what: Sealing finished devices in foil pouches with desiccant to protect against humidity, then labeling and boxing.
packaging.how: Devices are pouched with desiccant, labeled with lot number and expiry, and packed into kits.
packaging.why_matters: Humidity is the main environmental threat to lateral-flow stability; desiccant and sealed pouches extend shelf life.
applications: Sealing devices in foil pouches with desiccant
Kit labeling with lot and expiry

faq.a: It absorbs residual moisture to protect reagent stability and extend shelf life.

stability.name: Stability & Shelf Life
stability.what: Confirming a test performs consistently across its labeled shelf life and storage range.
stability.how: Real-time and accelerated stability studies validate performance at temperature and humidity extremes before shelf life is assigned.
stability.why_matters: Stability data underpins the labeled shelf life and the no-cold-chain advantage of colloidal-gold tests.
applications: Confirming performance across the labeled shelf life
limitations: Accelerated aging predicts but does not replace real-time data

faq.a: Confirming a test performs consistently across its storage range and shelf life.

qc.name: Quality Control
qc.what: Lot-level testing against reference panels before release.
qc.how: Each lot is tested for sensitivity, specificity and precision against known positive and negative samples; the internal control line validates each individual device.
qc.why_matters: QC ensures batch-to-batch consistency and catches failures before shipment.
limitations: QC samples may not cover all real-world matrices

faq.q: What is the internal control line for?
faq.a: It validates each device — distinguishing a true negative from a failed test.

oem-development.what: Turning a buyer specification — analyte, cut-off, packaging, branding — into a production-ready SKU.
oem-development.how: Custom formulations are developed, then re-validated for cut-off, sensitivity and specificity before release.
oem-development.why_matters: OEM customization must be re-validated — changing cut-off or format changes performance, so each custom SKU is qualified independently.
